title: Andy Kirk, Jr.
summary: Andy Kirk Jr. was the best young saxophonist around, practiced at home while Bird visited the Kirk family.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: This brings up a couple of questions. Andy Kirk, Jr., is mentioned, and of course he’s the son of Andy Kirk. I want you to talk a little bit more about him than what I’ve heard about him or seen about him in the literature. It mentions that he was a good player. I just want to know more about him and what happened in his life, as far as you know.

He was a tall, thin, young guy. A couple – maybe he was a year-and-a-half older than me, or two years older than me. So when I came into Theodore Roosevelt High School, he was a senior. So I was just there with him one year before he graduated. But I was around him a lot. I’d go around. He lived right around the corner from me. I’d go up and sit in his room and listen to him practice. He was the best saxophone player around, for his age. He played more than everybody, Sonny, all of them. None of them, to me, could touch Andy.
Who was all of them, besides Sonny?

John Gill, Percy France, all these guys from around New York, everybody. Nobody could touch Andy, Jr. He was bad. Even Bird used to come up and sit in the room and listen to Andy practice, because I remember one night I was having dinner, and Andy called me and he said, “Hey Jackie.” He said, “If you want to come around here,” he said, “Bird’s going to be here in a little while. Coming up to see my dad, man, if you want to come.” I said, “Yeah, I’ll be right around.” So I ate, ran around, and Bird was there.
So the Bird connection to the Kirk family was from . . .
. . . when he played with Andy Kirk.
Yeah, right, back in those days, and then he discovers the son, who’s extraordinary.
